traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Sarcobataceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; blades linear; stipules absent; plants monoecious or dioecious; ovary half inferior; stems woody; flowers solitary or in catkins; perianth tepals or absent; stamens 1 to 4; carpels 2. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.growth_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): shrubs, deciduous, much-branched (the family holds only Sarcobatus, so the genus account is the family's).

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): shrubs.

traits.life_span.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): a native flowering perennial (phanerophyte).

traits.leaf_habit.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): shrubs, deciduous.

traits.stem_posture.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): stems erect, much-branched, not jointed.

traits.spines.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): long shoots bear leaves and axillary thorns, thorns 1(-2) per node.

traits.short_shoots.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): stems dimorphic: long shoots elongate, short shoots clustered, budlike, bearing leaves.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): leaves mostly alternate on long shoots (sometimes opposite proximally) or clustered on short shoots.

traits.leaf_division.note: Kept from the library family file (Watson and Dallwitz DELTA data): leaves simple; FNA's blade description agrees.

traits.leaf_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): blade linear, nearly terete to somewhat flattened, succulent.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): blade linear.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): apex obtuse (mucronate).

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): margins entire.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): leaves sessile.

traits.stipules.note: German Wikipedia, 'Sarcobatus' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): no stipules (Nebenblätter sind keine vorhanden). File kept.

traits.sexual_system.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): shrubs monoecious. German Wikipedia: mostly monoecious, rarely dioecious; FEIS: some say monoecious, others generally monoecious but occasionally dioecious.

traits.ovary_position.note: German Wikipedia, 'Sarcobatus' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): two carpels united into a partly inferior (teilweise unterständig) ovary. File kept.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): staminate inflorescence a terminal, pedunculate, cylindric spike of 10-40 spirally arranged flowers (German Wikipedia: catkin-like); pistillate flowers solitary or paired in leaf axils.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): staminate spike of 10-40 flowers.

traits.flowering_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): staminate spikes terminal, distal to the axillary pistillate flowers.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): pistillate 'perianth' accrescent, adnate, cuplike; staminate flowers: perianth absent. File kept.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): anthers caducous, (1-)2-4(-5), almost sessile, under a peltate rhombic scarious scale; German Wikipedia: mostly two to four, rarely one or five.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): stigmas 2; German Wikipedia: two carpels. File kept.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): fruits achenes, with a broad wing from the flaring perianth.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): perianth accrescent, flaring to form a wing in fruit; wing sometimes red-tinged, veiny, broad, margins lobed and undulate.
